subject: history
title: AQA GCSE History — America 1840–1895: Expansion and Consolidation
subtitle: MCQ revision from 5 exam sittings
description: Multiple-choice revision questions covering the AQA GCSE History topic America 1840–1895: Expansion and Consolidation. Questions are drawn from factual content in model answers from five exam sittings (June 2022, June 2023, June 2024, November 2020, November 2021).

data.question: What was a danger faced by travellers crossing the Plains before 1865?
data.answer: Snow blizzards in the mountains
options: Snow blizzards in the mountains
Frequent volcanic eruptions
Attacks by Confederate soldiers
Poisonous insect swarms

data.question: What happened to the Donner party while crossing the Plains?
data.answer: They camped for winter, ran out of food, and survived by eating those who had died
options: They camped for winter, ran out of food, and survived by eating those who had died
They found a shortcut to California that halved their journey time
They were rescued by the US Cavalry before running out of supplies
They turned back and returned to the eastern states

data.question: What experience did the Gould family have crossing the Plains in 1862?
data.answer: They found 11 wagons that had been plundered by Plains Indians with the families killed
options: They found 11 wagons that had been plundered by Plains Indians with the families killed
They were caught in a tornado that destroyed their wagon and supplies
They discovered gold and became wealthy overnight
They were rescued by a friendly band of Sioux who guided them west

data.question: How did cotton production in the South change during the Civil War?
data.answer: It fell from 4 million bales in 1861 to 300,000 bales in 1865
options: It fell from 4 million bales in 1861 to 300,000 bales in 1865
It rose from 2 million to 6 million bales as demand increased
It remained steady at 4 million bales throughout the war
It fell from 10 million to 1 million bales over the same period

A military fort to defend against Indian attacks

options: Adobe bricks
Limestone blocks
Oak timber

data.answer: They sent an advanced pioneer band and divided into smaller groups led by a captain

data.question: What did the Pacific Railways Act of 1861 do?
data.answer: Gave railway companies land to sell to fund railroad building
options: Gave railway companies land to sell to fund railroad building
Made all railroad travel free for homesteaders
Banned railroads from being built across Indian lands
Created a federal tax to fund railway construction

data.question: How much land did the Homestead Act of 1862 provide and at what cost?
data.answer: 160 acres for $10
options: 160 acres for $10
40 acres for $5
320 acres for $50
640 acres for $100

data.question: What did the Timber and Culture Act of 1873 require homesteaders to do to receive extra land?
data.answer: Plant 40 acres with trees on the new land
options: Plant 40 acres with trees on the new land
Build a permanent wooden house within one year
Clear 40 acres of forest within the first season
Fence the entire 160-acre plot within two years

data.question: What was the purpose of the Fort Laramie Treaty of 1851?
data.answer: To keep Indians away from homesteaders by giving each tribe a hunting area
options: To keep Indians away from homesteaders by giving each tribe a hunting area
To force all Plains Indians onto reservations in Oklahoma
To ban white settlement west of the Mississippi River
To grant US citizenship to all Plains Indians

data.question: Who was elected US President in November 1860, triggering the secession crisis?
data.answer: Abraham Lincoln
options: Abraham Lincoln
Andrew Johnson
Ulysses S. Grant
Stephen A. Douglas

data.question: How did the Tariff of 1828 affect the Southern states?
data.answer: It made European imports more expensive to protect Northern industries
options: It made European imports more expensive to protect Northern industries
It banned all cotton exports to Europe
It taxed Southern exports to the North
It made Southern manufactured goods cheaper in Europe

data.question: What did the Dawes Act of 1887 do to Native American lands?
data.answer: Divided remaining Indian lands into 160-acre plots, most of which went to white settlers
options: Divided remaining Indian lands into 160-acre plots, most of which went to white settlers
Returned all tribal lands to Native American ownership
Created new permanent reservations in the Black Hills
Abolished the reservation system entirely

data.question: What happened in the Black Hills in 1874?
data.answer: Gold miners invaded the Black Hills, sacred to the Sioux
options: Gold miners invaded the Black Hills, sacred to the Sioux
The Sioux signed a peace treaty with the US government
The transcontinental railroad was completed through the hills
A major buffalo herd was exterminated by the US Army

data.question: What did the Plains Indians use buffalo for?
data.answer: Food, clothes, shoes, and tipis
options: Food, clothes, shoes, and tipis
Food only, they used other animals for clothing
Religious ceremonies only, not for daily needs

data.question: Why did buffalo hunters kill the buffalo on the Plains?
data.answer: They wanted the skins, not the meat, and destroyed whole herds
options: They wanted the skins, not the meat, and destroyed whole herds
They hunted only for meat to feed the army
They were paid by the US government to exterminate all buffalo
They hunted buffalo for sport and competition

data.answer: He did not sign a bill to protect the buffalo, allowing the killing to continue
options: He did not sign a bill to protect the buffalo, allowing the killing to continue
He signed a law making buffalo hunting illegal
He ordered the US Army to protect the remaining buffalo herds
He established a national buffalo reserve on the Plains

data.question: By when were the southern plains buffalo herds gone?
data.answer: By the end of 1875
options: By the end of 1875
By the end of 1865
By the end of 1885
By the end of 1890

data.answer: They attacked when Indians stayed in one place and conserved food
options: They attacked when Indians stayed in one place and conserved food
They stopped all fighting during winter months
They only fought in summer when conditions were better
They negotiated peace treaties every winter

data.question: What did the US government do to attract settlers to the West?
data.answer: They encouraged a belief in Manifest Destiny to inspire people to travel west
options: They encouraged a belief in Manifest Destiny to inspire people to travel west
